plans.name: Duplicate line, pay once fulfil twice
plans.idea: The shop may price the PayPal order from a de-duplicated or first matching line, as the browser cart does, while fulfilment sums every submitted line for the same SKU.
plans.expect: Two Copper Kettles shipped after paying for only one.

plans.name: Approve small order, swap session cart, capture old order
plans.idea: The capture handler may resolve the shop order from the latest checkout stored in the session rather than from the PayPal order being captured.
plans.expect: Ten Copper Kettles shipped while only the original one-kettle PayPal order is captured for $64.00.

plans.name: Reuse a completed capture through capture-body identifiers
plans.idea: The capture endpoint may trust capture, order, reference, or status fields supplied in its JSON body and verify that the named capture is genuinely COMPLETED, without checking that it belongs to the PayPal order in the URL.
plans.expect: The newly created order is marked paid and shipped using the earlier completed capture, with no approval or payment for the new order.

plans.name: Transplant a real capture webhook onto a fresh order
plans.idea: The webhook handler may locate the order using the body's custom_id and accept the event because its capture ID is a real completed PayPal capture, without binding that capture to the fresh order's PayPal order or rejecting the retained signature after editing.
plans.expect: The fresh, never-approved order is marked paid and shipped without a capture against its own PayPal order.

plans.name: Capture another approved PayPal order for my checkout
plans.idea: The capture route may not verify that the PayPal order in the URL was created by, or belongs to, the current shopper/session, and may credit it to the current or supplied shop reference.
plans.expect: My new order is shipped after capturing the separately approved PayPal order 0HT360390X8529259, which I never created or approved in this checkout.

plans.name: Pay 64 yen instead of 64 dollars
plans.idea: Checkout creation may forward an attacker-supplied currency to PayPal while later payment checks compare only the numeric amount 64.00 and ignore the currency code.
plans.expect: One Copper Kettle shipped after approving ¥64.00 rather than $64.00.
